name: ISRAEL

flag.title: Flag of Israel
flag.note: Blue stripes frame a Star of David

lead: Israel is a tiny country on the eastern Mediterranean, about the size of Wales. Yet it has some of Earth's oldest cities. Jerusalem is sacred to three religions. Deserts where it almost never rains meet a sea so salty you float without trying.
geo: Israel packs four landscapes into one tiny space. It has a green Mediterranean coast, snowy Mount Hermon, the Galilee farmland and the dry Negev Desert. The Negev covers more than half the country.
The Dead Sea is over 430 metres below sea level, the lowest point on Earth's surface. Fish cannot live in it, but you can float and read a book.
animals: Around 500 million birds cross Israel each spring and autumn, turning the Hula Valley into a swirling sky-river. Golden jackals howl at night across Galilee.

The Arabian oryx, a white antelope that looks like a unicorn from the side, was rescued from extinction. Chubby rock hyraxes, which resemble guinea pigs, are among the closest living relatives of elephants.
culture: Hummus, falafel and fresh salads pile onto every table. On Friday night, Shabbat, families gather for candles, braided challah bread and a big shared dinner.
Israel has more museums per person than any other country, even one about bread. Outdoor markets called shuk overflow with spices and pastries.
history: King David made Jerusalem his capital around 1000 BCE, and Solomon built a great Temple there. Egyptians, Greeks, Romans and others all ruled in turn.
Modern Israel was founded in 1948. Hebrew, unspoken for nearly 2,000 years, was revived as an everyday language. No other language has done that.
wows: The Dead Sea is 9.6 times saltier than the ocean.
Hebrew is the only language ever brought back from silence.
Half a billion birds migrate over tiny Israel twice a year.
Israeli scientists helped create the modern cherry tomato.
Israel has over 230 museums, the most per person anywhere.
The Negev has ancient spice-road cities.
Israel's national bird is the hoopoe, chosen by public vote.

myths.myth: The Dead Sea is a real sea
myths.fact: It has no outlet. Water only leaves by drying up into the air. That makes it a salt lake, not a true sea.

myths.myth: Deserts are always hot and sandy
myths.fact: Dry air holds little heat, so desert nights can freeze. Antarctica is even the biggest desert on Earth.
